items.name: Codex conductor
items.summary: Start, inspect, steer and interrupt native Codex work in an installation-owned profile.
setup: Run borg auth codex on this machine, then borg doctor.
Use the installed conductor with your own project path and a unique work ID.
limitations: Your provider account, allowance and live machine admission are required. A selected conductor is not a running agent.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Machine and account router
items.summary: Choose among your configured Codex lanes using live capacity, account identity, work claims and allowance.
setup: Configure your own machine/account lanes in conductors/config.json.
Verify current capacity and claims collectors before dispatch; follow conductor/INTEGRATION.md.
limitations: Remote tool enrollment does not add conductor lanes. Unknown capacity or account state fails admission.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Grok conductor
items.summary: Run the bundled Grok bridge with interruption and same-session resume.
setup: Install and sign in to a compatible Grok CLI in your own dedicated profile.
Configure its binary, profile, version, private state and loopback port in conductors/config.json; follow the provider setup guide.
Qualify the actual CLI and create its readiness receipt before starting the bundled bridge.
limitations: Grok CLI and credentials are not installed by BORG. The bridge is not part of Codex allowance routing.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Claude launch adapter
items.summary: Launch bounded Claude Code headless work through the provider launch bus.
setup: Install Claude Code and complete its native sign-in with your own account.
Set the Claude binary and enable the provider in your private conductor configuration.
Use the documented launch packet with a bounded work ID, prompt and project path.
limitations: This adapter does not provide native thread status, mid-turn steering or provider allowance routing.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Provider launch bus
items.summary: Send a common work packet to the selected Codex, Grok or Claude backend and retain a launch receipt.
setup: Configure the provider you will use, then validate its native readiness.
Submit a bounded packet through the launch-bus CLI; inspect the provider result as well as the launch receipt.
limitations: A launch receipt is not completed work. Provider capabilities differ.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Agent Inbox
items.summary: Authenticated identities, grants, leased messages, assignments and shared discoveries.
setup: Use the installation-owned Inbox; create scoped identities for your agents.
Verify a send, recipient read and acknowledgment using those identities.
limitations: Each installation starts with its own Hub and empty records; selecting Inbox does not federate multiple Hubs.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Beads work tracking
items.summary: Durable projects, owned tasks, dependencies and acceptance evidence.
setup: Use the installed borg home/bin/bd wrapper to access this installation’s work store.
Create a project, claim work and record acceptance before closing it.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Fleet context extension
items.summary: Public source for a bounded view of machine, account and work observations from your own collectors.
setup: Build or connect your own telemetry and account/work collectors using the documented source contract.
Embed the fleet context reader with explicit owner-controlled sources; the default source list is empty.
Verify fresh coverage and actual work ownership before using its observations.
limitations: Source extension only: the installer does not deploy collectors or operational dashboards. Missing and stale observations stay unknown.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Memory maintenance scripts
items.summary: Source for scoped ingestion, consolidation, decay and cleanup under your own retention policy.
setup: Review the shipped script and its configuration/help before running against your data.
Set your own retention, backup, allowed sources and scheduling; verify a bounded operation first.
limitations: Scripts are included; historical schedules and private ingestion sources are not. The background graph feed is a separate service.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Provider login handles
items.summary: Keep nonsecret provider metadata and route an agent to the correct native login or consent screen.
setup: Configure provider names, HTTPS login URLs and intended scopes in the private borg-context/credentials.json registry.
Discover credential_ tools and verify the returned native login handoff.
limitations: Handles contain metadata only. They do not hold credentials, proxy authenticated APIs or prove current provider authorization.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Multi-machine connector
items.summary: Route files, commands, jobs and browser tools to explicitly enrolled machines.
setup: Install each target independently and verify its borg_identity.
Establish trusted SSH, then enroll its exact owner, home and instance ID with borg fleet add.
Verify fleet_hosts and perform a reversible tool call on the selected machine.
limitations: Enrollment is explicit. Memory is not replicated between machines. Shared desktop resources remain serialized.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Native browser tools
items.summary: BORG-owned browser sessions with inspect, click, navigation and durable operation receipts.
setup: Use borg tools browser_ to discover the installed schema.
Open an allowed page and verify a reversible interaction.
limitations: Browser runtime is included even if this planning option is unselected. Account sign-in and website permissions remain yours.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: macOS desktop tools
items.summary: Inspect and operate native apps in an interactive macOS session.
setup: Grant the OS permissions required by your chosen apps and tools.
Use ui_permissions and a reversible native app action to verify access.
limitations: Requires an interactive macOS session. One physical desktop cannot serve independent simultaneous focus actions.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Extraction LoRA adapters
items.summary: Three shipped adapter weight sets and model cards for local extraction research.
setup: Inspect borg adapters list.
On Apple Silicon, use borg adapters prepare only when you want the separately downloaded, pinned MLX base models.
Run your own held-out evaluation and real-pipeline canary before any promotion.
limitations: Inactive by default. Preparation does not enable extraction or establish semantic quality.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

items.name: Training and evaluation
items.summary: Private dataset builders, training chains, held-out exams and promotion canaries.
setup: Set a private dataset and checkpoint budget; use only data you are permitted to train on.
Read the training and adapter model cards before running an isolated experiment.
Keep the daily memory pipeline separate from resource-heavy training.
limitations: No unattended training or promotion is enabled. Hardware allowances are not measured training minimums.
items.license: BORG implementation: MIT; provider terms apply

sizing.memory_units: GB planning units (decimal); purchase the next suitable hardware tier
sizing.disk_units: GB of free SSD space, not total drive size
sizing.default_model: qwen3:4b Q4_K_M + nomic-embed-text, local extraction only

sources.name: BORG hardware guide and locked artifacts

notes: These values are conservative planning allowances, not measured minimums, throughput promises or dispatch admission.
Default local extraction uses one parallel Ollama request; cloud coding agents do not load frontier model weights on the host.
The fact allowance includes vectors, payload, graph/history and headroom. Actual payload/index/retention size varies. It is not a Qdrant benchmark.
External services are assumed to run elsewhere. Add their separately measured host requirements if you co-locate them.
The worker profile retains the complete dependency package; it saves running memory/model services, not all runtime disk space.
Training adds a planning reserve only; profile the exact base model, sequence, layers, batch, dataset and checkpoints.
